blocks.note: PHASE 3 (§L1) — an agent's question, in the thread, AS A FORM: radio buttons for single choice, checkboxes for multiple, inputs for the rest. A person with commenter rights or above can answer; when `to` is set the card says whom it is waiting for and only they may submit

Submit goes through the outbox like every other write, so the card locks at once (an optimistic patch on the message) and nothing waits for the server. Answered, cancelled and expired all lock in place: the chosen values, 'Answered by Panth · 10:42', and the answer also arrives as your own reply bubble

PHASE 5 (§N): the card does not care WHO asked. A person's question (from the composer's builder) notifies, badges and locks exactly like an agent's; the asker — person or agent — and board admins can take an open one back, which locks it as Cancelled

blocks.note: PHASE 5 (§N1) — the composer's dialog for asking a question. Four starting points fill the fields in; up to 10 fields (single / multi / text / long text / number / yes-no / date), each with a label, an options editor (add, reorder, remove) and Required. Who should answer picks people AND agents (empty = anyone on the board); Blocking puts ❓ Waiting on the ticket; Expires is never / an hour / a day / a week

The preview IS the Question card, rendered inert — what is on the right is exactly what the thread will show. Ask goes through the outbox like any message (the entry id is the message id), so the card appears at once and rolls back if the server refuses. A draft that passes the dialog is a question questionAsk accepts: the validation is the shared one

blocks.note: PHASE 3 (§L2) — at the top of the right pane, above the fields. A progress bar per list; the item being worked on (doing) is highlighted with a spinner, failed items are red with their note. Editors and the list's owner can tick an item by hand — the same command the agent calls, and it leaves no thread line

PHASE 5 (§N2): + New list takes a title and the items — paste a plan and each line becomes one. Per list: rename, add an item, edit it in place, drag (or ↑ ↓) to reorder, delete an item, delete the list. Per item: click the status to walk todo → doing → done, or use its ⋯ menu for skipped and failed (failed asks for a note first)

Who may (§N2): editors and admins, and the list's OWNER — which is how an agent keeps its plan while a person still ticks an item off, and how a person's own list works with no agent anywhere. Commenters and viewers get the same pane, read-only: what you may not do is not drawn rather than failing on click. Every change goes through the outbox; one item's status is tasklistItemUpdate (no thread line), anything structural is a whole-list tasklistSet

PHASE 3 (§L3) — ONE component and one derivation (AgentHealth) behind every dot in the app: the drawer header, board cards, agent avatars, People & roles and the Agents page. A card asks for a dot; it never computes one

ONE LISTENER PER BOARD on agentStatus feeds all of them, and the clock is recomputed every 15 s — a quarter of the beat interval — so a 'working' agent that stopped beating goes red by itself, with nothing written anywhere

@ → people AND agents on this board, matched by name or email, agents with their badge and description; # → Typesense prefix search on key and title; / → slash commands (/assign, /due, /stage, /ask). Drag, drop or paste many files at once, each with its own progress bar and ✕ to remove before sending; a message can be files only. Draft kept per ticket in IndexedDB

PHASE 5 (§N1): ❓ opens the QUESTION BUILDER — the same card an agent posts, built by hand. It is shown to anyone who may comment (not just editors), and /ask is the same door from the keyboard: the slash line runs when you send it
drag to reorder, colour swatch, category (stages); removing one in use asks where its tickets go
